author: muse-b3
covers: Hand recipe (kind repro-steps) for SC-04 (the refusal leg), authored by muse-b3 as author of record (GB-1555 + CB-0824 SC-foundations runway) from the fixer's check file: /Users/dutch/.zuko/quality/CHECK-SC-04.md (seat B2, branch v1/sc-foundations, build 10c2e066c18b27e839e8f4d72e2400fe72f8b961, parent exactly 0f00e554d — shared landing with SC-00, one commit, both tickets; FPV at dossier line 1052). Defect: parseQuantity (server/lib/conkay/compiler/units.js) coerces a bare number to SI whenever the caller names an expected dimension (flagged coercedBare) across all three input forms (number, unit-less string, unit-less object), and the flag had NO production consumer in the deployed tree — a bare length: 4 on a solver input was silently treated as 4 metres, against the catalogue's adversarial text riding every solver row ('bare number on a dimensional input refused unless the unit is declared; non-SI inputs echoed and converted exactly'). Fix: the refusal lives ONLY at the solve.direct boundary — validateDirectInputs in server/lib/conkay/solve-direct.js: geometry keys take their dimension from the compiler's own paramDim, position axes are length, TYPED_PROPS props carry their declared dimensions, load fields are dimensional by contract; a value whose parseQuantity(value, dim).coercedBare is true is refused invalid_input naming the field, the dimension, and the remedy; the bridge's direct mode shares the one validator, so the refusal cannot be routed around by choosing an entry. parseQuantity itself is UNTOUCHED, by design of record: the IR compiler's bare coercion is deliberate and tested (chat-driven design authoring depends on it — position {x:0,y:0,z:0}, mass: 1.5), so the refusal is scoped to the solver-input boundary, never a global parseQuantity change. Evidence of record: suite server/tests/conkay-sc04-refusal.test.js 13/13 PASS in the built tree; landed extract @ 10c2e066c runs SC-04 + SC-00 + SC-05 suites 28/28 PASS; pristine control (deployed main extract) fails at import (solve-direct.js absent — no refusal seam exists pre-fix); non-SI inputs '4000 mm' and '13.123359580052493 ft' reproduce the '4 m' run's maxDeflection bit-for-bit. Named limits, carried entire: dimension knowledge comes from the compiler's tables — a dimensional value in an untyped prop key is the solver's domain and is not policed at this seam (geometry, position, typed props, and loads — the catalogue's dimensional surfaces — are); refusal inside design authoring, if ever wanted, is a separate ticket against the IR compiler, not this seam.
discriminator: Pre-fix transcript (from CHECK-SC-04.md; premise executed against the deployed build 21303b4672): no refusal seam exists — the suite fails at import on the deployed build (solve-direct.js absent), parseQuantity's coercedBare flag has no production consumer (its only reader is a test asserting the coercion on the chat/IR path), and a bare length: 4 on a solver input is silently accepted as 4 metres. Post-fix: 13/13 PASS — bare refused in all three forms at the direct boundary only, and the same bare length: 4 still compiles and solves through openDesign (the authoring coercion pinned intact by the contrast leg).
steps: At the solve.direct boundary, submit the beam's length as bare 4 (number), "4" (unit-less string), and {value:4} (unit-less object): each is refused invalid_input naming node.geometry.length, its dimension, and the remedy.

Submit a bare load (pointLoad without a unit): refused naming loadCases.LC1.loads.pointLoad; a bare typed prop (mass: 2) and a bare position axis are refused likewise; the MCP bridge refuses identically; a missing node is refused, not crashed.
Submit "4000 mm" and "13.123359580052493 ft": both solve, and maxDeflection reproduces the "4 m" run bit-for-bit; {value:4000, unit:"mm"} passes.
Submit a dimensionless prop bare: it passes. Submit a wrong-dimension unit ("4 kg" for length): it errors honestly as a bad input, not a refusal.
Contrast leg: the same bare length: 4 still compiles and solves through openDesign — the IR-authoring coercion is intact and parseQuantity is untouched.
title: A bare number on a dimensional solver input is refused at the solve.direct boundary, while design authoring keeps its deliberate coercion
